This order shall dispose of two petitions i.e. CRM-M-20012-2024 and CRM-M-52217 52217-2024.
The petitioners are seeking the concession of bail under Section 39 Cr.P.C read with Section 437 (6)
Cr.P.C. in case FIR No.0332 332 dated 25.07.2022 under Sections 406, 420, 120-B, B, 467, 468, 471 IPC, 1860 registered at Police Station Model Town, Panipat, District Panipat.

The same is taken on record subject to all just exceptions.

Learned counsel for the petitioner(s petitioner s) contend that the petitioner(s) have been falsely implicated in the present case al along with other co-accused accused for allegedly cheating the complainants by luring them to invest in a company on the pretext of getting higher returns.

While drawing the attention of this Court ourt to the FIR annexed as Annexure P-1, P learned earned counsel submit that the petitioners' false implication in the case in hand finds credence from the fact that even during investigation, investigation no recovery of any money stated to have been given in cash by the complainants had been affected from them.

Learned counsel for the petitioner(s) petitioner have further submitted that after the petitioners i.e. Monika Sharma and Vijay Sharma were arrested on 18.03.2023 and 21.08.2022 respectively, not only had the investigation been completed and challan presented; but even charges stand framed, however, tthe he possibility of the trial concluding in the near future did not arise since as many as 116 prosecution witnesses have been cited.

It has been still further submitted that after the commencement of prosecution evidence on 21.12.2023 21.12.2023, the complainant and the other alleged victims have failed to put in their appearance despite issuance of non bailable warrants against them.
In support support, learned counsel have drawn the attention of this Court ourt to zimni orders annexed as Annexure P-5.

Learned ned counsel have further submitted that petitioner- petitioner-Monika Monika is not even the prime accused in the crime in question and has been implicated in the case in hand 2 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:147051 only for being the wife of the main accused pe petitioner-Vijay.

It has been submitted that the co-accused co accused Ajay Sharma, Parmod Sharma, Savita Sharma and Vijay Pal Sharma have since been extended the concession of bbail ail vide order dated 05.09.2024 05.09.202 Annexure P-6.

Learned counsel submit that in the aforementioned circumstances, no useful purpose would be served in keeping the petitioners in custody in a case triable by magistrate and hence, they be enlarged on bail.

sentences.text: Per contra, learned  l State counsel, on instructions  instructions, has vehemently opposed the prayer and submissions made by the counsel opposite.

Learned State counsel, has submitted that all the accused including the petitioners belong to the same family, and had duped and cheated a number of gullible persons, who had been given false assurance of high returns on their investments, however, no interest had been given as per the assurance, rather the entire money invested in the company of the petitioners had been swallowed by each of them.
Learned State counsel, has, however, not disputed that the challan has already been presented, even the charges already stand framed and the case is at the stage of prosecution evidence.

The factum of co co-accused accused been extended the concession of bail has also not been di disputed by the learned State tate counsel; it has however been submitted that the accused Vijay Sharma is the prime accused, and in case the petitioners are extended the concession of bail, stringent conditions may be put on them..
Learned S State counsel has further her apprised this Court ourt that four out of 116 witnesses already stand examined.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the relevant material placed on record.
record 3 of 5 Neutral Citation No:=2024:PHHC:147051 CRM-M-20012
The petitioners Monika Monika Sharma and Vijay Sharma have been in custody since 18.03.2023 and 21.08.2022 respectively in a magisterial trial.
The conclusion of the trial is going to take long time as 112 prosecution witnesses still remain to be examined.

In the facts and circumstances as enumerated hereinabove, and without commenting any further on the merits, the present petitions are allowed and the petitioners are ordered to be released on bail on his furnishing bail bonds/surety bonds to the satisfaction satisfaction of the learned trial Court/Duty Magistrate/CJM concerned subject to the following conditions:
conditions:-

( i) The petitioners shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any persons acquainted with the facts of the case, so as to dissuade ssuade him to disclose such facts to the Court or to any other authority.
(ii) The petitioners shall remain present before the Court on each of the dates fixed for hearing of the case.
(iii) The petitioners shall not absent themselves or seek unnecessary adjournments ments from the Court proceedings.

(iv) The petitioners shall surrender their passport, if any, (if already not surrendered)
surrendered).
